Require a money-flow confirmation via an explicit cross: df['mfi_14'] > 50 AND df['mfi_14'] on the prior bar <= 50. Exit on risk if df['roc_5'] > 1.02 OR df['close'] < df['sma_50']. Take profit when df['roc_10'] < 0.94, and also exit if df['mfi_14'] < 45 to avoid holding through distribution.

L1_medium.summary: Reclaim of Bollinger midline with OBV accumulation, exiting at bands or adverse ROC.
L1_medium.query: The strategy triggers on a recovery back above the trend baseline: df['close'] > df['bb_middle_20'] AND df['close'] on the prior bar <= df['bb_middle_20'] on the prior bar (explicit cross above the middle band). Require accumulation and controlled volatility at the same time: df['obv'] > df['obv'] on the prior bar shifted by 10 bars AND df['vsumd_10'] > 0 AND df['std_20'] < 0.05. Add a momentum sanity check to avoid late entries by enforcing df['rsi_14'] > 45 AND df['rsi_14'] < 70. Take profit when df['close'] > df['bb_upper_20'] OR when df['rsv_14'] > 0.85. Stop out when df['close'] < df['bb_lower_20'] OR when df['roc_5'] > 1.03.

L1_medium.summary: Early momentum bursts via short-horizon beta and volume thrust, exiting on fast ROC targets.
L1_medium.query: Buy when momentum ignites quickly, even at the cost of more whipsaws. Trigger an entry if (df['beta_3'] < -0.012 AND df['vsumd_5'] > 0.60) OR (df['qtlu_20'] > 0.020 AND df['vma_20'] < 0.80), and require df['rsi_7'] crosses above 55 as the final go-signal (df['rsi_7'] > 55 AND df['rsi_7'].shift(1) <= 55). Exit immediately on fixed risk outcomes: take profit if df['roc_3'] < 0.96, and stop out if df['roc_3'] > 1.04. Also exit when df['rsi_7'] crosses below 45 (df['rsi_7'] < 45 AND df['rsi_7'].shift(1) >= 45) to cut failed momentum early.

L1_medium.summary: Trend-aligned stochastic cross with low-volatility filter and tight ATR risk exits.
L1_medium.query: Enter a position only when all of the following are true: df['close'] > df['sma_100'] AND df['ema_20'] > df['sma_100'] AND df['std_20'] < 0.03. Require a momentum turn by a defined cross: df['stoch_k_14'] > df['stoch_d_14'] AND yesterday df['stoch_k_14'] <= yesterday df['stoch_d_14']. Add a quality filter to avoid chasing: df['rsi_14'] > 45 AND df['rsi_14'] < 65. Take profit when df['close'] >= df['ema_20'] + 1.5 * df['atr_14']. Stop out when df['close'] <= df['ema_20'] - 1.0 * df['atr_14'] OR when a bearish cross occurs (df['stoch_k_14'] < df['stoch_d_14'] AND yesterday df['stoch_k_14'] >= yesterday df['stoch_d_14']).

L1_medium.summary: Capitulation-wick reversal confirmed by RSI and price reclaim, with tight ROC risk exits.
L1_medium.query: The strategy seeks low-frequency rebound trades after a downside flush but only with strong confirmation. Enter when df['rsi_14'] > 32 AND df['rsi_14'].shift(1) <= 32 (RSI cross up), AND df['close'] > df['sma_10'] AND df['close'].shift(1) <= df['sma_10'].shift(1) (price cross above SMA), AND (df['klow2'] > 0.60 OR df['ksft2'] > 0.20), AND df['atr_14'] < 0.03 * df['close'], AND df['vma_20'] < 1.05 AND df['vma_20'] > 0.80. Take profit when df['roc_10'] < 0.95 OR df['close'] > df['bb_middle_20']. Stop loss when df['roc_3'] > 1.02 OR df['close'] < df['bb_lower_20']. If both take-profit and stop-loss conditions are true on the same bar, prioritize the stop-loss action.

L1_medium.summary: Fast breakout entry using RSV surge and positive volume-diff confirmation, with wider ROC exits.
L1_medium.query: Buy when momentum ignites quickly and participation confirms it. Enter if (df['rsv_10'] > 0.80 AND df['rsv_10'].shift(1) <= 0.80) OR (df['close'] > df['bb_upper_20'] AND df['close'].shift(1) <= df['bb_upper_20'].shift(1)); then require df['vsumd_10'] > 0.40 AND df['std_20'] > 0.02 AND df['imax_20'] > 0.80. Take profit at a fixed threshold when df['roc_5'] < 0.90 OR when df['rsv_10'] > 0.92. Stop loss at a fixed threshold when df['roc_2'] > 1.05 OR when df['rsv_10'] < 0.60 AND df['rsv_10'].shift(1) >= 0.60 (RSV cross down). If take-profit and stop-loss trigger together, execute the stop-loss.

L1_medium.summary: Trend-filtered Bollinger reclaim with money-flow confirmation and tight ATR-based risk exits.
L1_medium.query: Risk management comes first: generate a buy signal only when df['sma_200'] < df['sma_100'] AND df['wvma_20'] < 1.20 AND df['mfi_14'] > 55. Require a confirmed reclaim by defining a bullish cross where df['close'] > df['bb_middle_20'] AND df['close'].shift(1) <= df['bb_middle_20'].shift(1). Add a price-location filter so df['close'] < df['bb_upper_20'] to avoid chasing extended moves. Generate an exit signal (stop-loss) when df['close'] <= df['bb_lower_20'] - 1.00 * df['atr_14']. Generate an exit signal (take-profit) when df['close'] >= df['bb_upper_20'] + 0.50 * df['atr_14'] OR df['rsi_14'] >= 72.

L1_medium.summary: Trend-filtered pullback entry using MFI cross, with tight ROC-based risk exits.
L1_medium.query: Enter a buy signal only when df['close'] > df['sma_200'] AND df['close'] < df['sma_50'] AND df['rsi_14'] < 40 AND df['vma_20'] < 0.95. Require a money-flow turn: df['mfi_14'] > 30 AND df['mfi_14'] from the prior bar <= 30 (a 30-level bullish cross). Generate a take-profit sell signal when df['roc_15'] < 0.96. Generate a stop-loss sell signal when df['roc_10'] > 1.02. Also generate an immediate risk-off sell signal if df['close'] < df['sma_200'] AND df['close'] from the prior bar >= df['sma_200'] (downward cross).

L1_medium.summary: Two-regime approach: low-volatility mean reversion and high-volatility trend entry with uniform risk exits.
L1_medium.query: First classify the regime on the current bar using df['std_20']: treat df['std_20'] < 0.02 as low-volatility, otherwise as high-volatility. In low-volatility, buy when df['close'] < df['bb_lower_20'] AND df['qtld_20'] < -0.03 AND df['rsi_14'] < 35. In high-volatility, buy when df['close'] > df['sma_50'] AND df['sumd_10'] > 0.20 AND df['cci_20'] > 0 AND df['cci_20'] from the prior bar <= 0 (0-line cross). For every bar, generate a take-profit sell signal when df['roc_10'] < 0.96 and a stop-loss sell signal when df['roc_10'] > 1.03. Also generate a defensive sell signal when df['close'] < df['sma_50'] AND df['close'] from the prior bar >= df['sma_50'].

L1_medium.summary: Regime-aware rules switch between correlation-backed momentum and discounted pullback recovery entries.
L1_medium.query: First classify the current bar as high-volatility when df['std_20'] >= 0.035; otherwise treat it as low-volatility. In high-volatility, enter when df['ma_50'] < 0.995 AND df['cord_20'] crosses above 0.20 (current df['cord_20'] > 0.20 AND prior df['cord_20'] <= 0.20) AND df['sumd_10'] > 0.20. In low-volatility, enter when df['min_30'] > 0.985 AND df['qtld_40'] < -0.030 AND df['rsi_14'] crosses above 35 (current df['rsi_14'] > 35 AND prior df['rsi_14'] <= 35). Use volatility-based sizing on the signal bar: if df['std_20'] < 0.025 use 100% allocation, else use 60% allocation. Risk management must use fixed thresholds: in high-volatility use take-profit +5.0% and stop-loss -2.5% from the entry close, while in low-volatility use take-profit +4.0% and stop-loss -1.8% from the entry close; additionally exit if df['cord_20'] crosses below 0.00 (current df['cord_20'] < 0.00 AND prior df['cord_20'] >= 0.00) OR if df['ma_50'] > 1.010.

L1_medium.summary: Uptrend dip-entry using quantile discount and stochastic cross, with volatility-based sizing.
L1_medium.query: This approach buys pullbacks inside an uptrend: require df['ma_50'] < 0.995 AND df['qtld_20'] < -0.015. Trigger the entry only when df['stoch_k_14'] crosses above df['stoch_d_14'] (today df['stoch_k_14'] > df['stoch_d_14'] AND yesterday df['stoch_k_14'] <= df['stoch_d_14']) AND df['stoch_k_14'] < 45. Set position size to 1.0 when df['std_20'] <= 0.040, otherwise cap position size at 0.5 when df['std_20'] > 0.040. Take profit when df['qtlu_20'] > 0.030 OR df['roc_10'] < 0.95 OR when df['stoch_k_14'] crosses below df['stoch_d_14'] while df['stoch_k_14'] > 80. Apply a fixed stop-loss when df['roc_5'] > 1.03 OR when df['std_20'] > 0.065.

L1_medium.summary: Pullback-reclaim entry in an EMA uptrend with volatility-gated sizing and dual exits.
L1_medium.query: This approach seeks pullback entries within an existing uptrend, then exits on momentum loss or fixed thresholds. Enter when df['close'] crosses above df['sma_10'] (df['close'] > df['sma_10'] AND df['close'].shift(1) <= df['sma_10'].shift(1)) while trend is positive (df['ema_20'] > df['ema_60']) and the bar reflects a discount to the recent average (df['ma_20'] > 1.01). Only allow entries when volatility is not extreme: df['std_20'] < 0.06. Set position size to 100% if df['std_20'] < 0.03, otherwise 60% if df['std_20'] is between 0.03 and 0.06 (inclusive of 0.03 and exclusive of 0.06). Exit when df['close'] crosses below df['sma_10'] (df['close'] < df['sma_10'] AND df['close'].shift(1) >= df['sma_10'].shift(1)) OR when volatility spikes to df['std_20'] > 0.08. Use fixed exits as well: take-profit when df['roc_7'] < 0.95 and stop-loss when df['roc_7'] > 1.03.

L1_medium.summary: Low-volatility mid-band reclaim with money-flow confirmation and tight quantile-based risk exits.
L1_medium.query: Enter when df['close'] crosses above df['bb_middle_20'] (df['close'] > df['bb_middle_20'] AND df['close'].shift(1) <= df['bb_middle_20'].shift(1)) AND df['std_20'] < 0.030 AND df['mfi_14'] > 55 AND df['vma_20'] < 0.90. Use a smaller position size (e.g., 50% of maximum) when df['std_20'] is between 0.020 and 0.030, and otherwise do not enter unless df['std_20'] < 0.020. Take profit when df['close'] crosses above df['bb_upper_20'] (df['close'] > df['bb_upper_20'] AND df['close'].shift(1) <= df['bb_upper_20'].shift(1)) OR when df['qtlu_20'] > 0.050. Cut risk immediately when df['qtld_20'] < -0.040 OR when df['close'] crosses below df['bb_middle_20'] (df['close'] < df['bb_middle_20'] AND df['close'].shift(1) >= df['bb_middle_20'].shift(1)). Add a volatility kill-switch exit: if df['std_20'] > 0.055, flatten regardless of other signals.

L1_medium.summary: Low-volatility pullback entry on SMA recapture with wick confirmation and tight ROC exits.
L1_medium.query: Enter a position when df['close'] crosses above df['sma_30'] (today df['close'] > df['sma_30'] AND yesterday df['close'] <= df['sma_30']). Require confirmation with df['std_20'] < 0.020 AND df['rsi_14'] > 40 AND df['mfi_14'] > 50. Also require a rejection-style candle via (df['klow2'] > 0.55 OR df['ksft2'] > 0.20). Take profit when df['roc_10'] < 0.960 OR when df['close'] crosses below df['sma_30'] (today df['close'] < df['sma_30'] AND yesterday df['close'] >= df['sma_30']). Stop loss when df['roc_5'] > 1.020.

L1_medium.summary: Slow trend-following entry with volume confirmation, filtered by low volatility and tight risk exits.
L1_medium.query: Enter when a bullish moving-average cross occurs: df['sma_20'] > df['sma_60'] AND the prior bar had df['sma_20'] <= df['sma_60']. Require additional confirmation that df['close'] > df['sma_60'] AND df['atr_14'] < 0.025 * df['close'] AND df['vma_20'] < 0.95. Also require (df['mfi_14'] > 55 OR df['cntd_10'] > 0.20). Exit when a bearish cross occurs (df['sma_20'] < df['sma_60'] AND the prior bar had df['sma_20'] >= df['sma_60']) OR when df['roc_5'] > 1.03 (stop-loss) OR when df['roc_10'] < 0.92 (take-profit).

L1_medium.summary: EMA-trend participation with price-volume alignment checks and volatility gating, plus dual profit/risk exits.
L1_medium.query: Prioritize risk first: exit when df['close'] crosses below df['ema_30'] (df['close'] < df['ema_30'] AND the prior bar had df['close'] >= df['ema_30']) OR when df['cord_20'] < -0.10. Use fixed thresholds as hard exits: stop-loss if df['roc_7'] > 1.05 and take-profit if df['qtlu_20'] > 0.07. Enter only when df['close'] crosses above df['ema_30'] (df['close'] > df['ema_30'] AND the prior bar had df['close'] <= df['ema_30']) AND df['ema_30'] > df['ema_100']. Require df['corr_20'] > 0.10 AND df['min_20'] < 0.985 AND df['mfi_14'] >= 45 AND df['mfi_14'] <= 65. Add a volatility gate so trades occur only if (df['std_20'] < 0.05 OR df['atr_14'] < 0.035 * df['close']).

L1_medium.summary: Mid-band reclaim with OBV confirmation and tight ROC-based profit and loss exits.
L1_medium.query: Enter when df['close'] crosses above df['bb_middle_20'] (df['close'] > df['bb_middle_20'] AND df['close'].shift(1) <= df['bb_middle_20'].shift(1)). Require df['rsi_14'] > 50 AND df['rsi_14'] < 65, df['std_20'] < 0.02, df['klen'] < 0.03, and df['obv'] > df['obv'].shift(5) on the same bar. Exit when df['close'] crosses below df['bb_middle_20'] (df['close'] < df['bb_middle_20'] AND df['close'].shift(1) >= df['bb_middle_20'].shift(1)) OR when df['roc_10'] < 0.96 as a take-profit OR when df['roc_5'] > 1.02 as a stop-loss. Add a safety exit if df['std_20'] >= 0.035 regardless of other signals.

L1_medium.summary: Slow trend confirmation via SMA cross with volatility filter and band-based risk exits.
L1_medium.query: The strategy prioritizes capital preservation by only entering on confirmed trend alignment and controlled volatility. Enter when a bullish cross occurs: df['sma_20'] > df['sma_60'] AND yesterday df['sma_20'] <= yesterday df['sma_60'], AND df['close'] > df['bb_middle_20'], AND df['std_20'] < 0.03, AND df['rsi_14'] > 52 AND df['rsi_14'] < 70. Exit immediately if a bearish cross occurs (df['sma_20'] < df['sma_60'] AND yesterday df['sma_20'] >= yesterday df['sma_60']) OR if df['close'] < df['bb_lower_20']. Apply fixed risk/return exits: take-profit when df['close'] >= df['sma_60'] * 1.06, and stop-loss when df['close'] <= df['sma_60'] * 0.97. Add a protective volatility-stop: exit if df['std_20'] >= 0.06.

L1_medium.summary: High-tempo breakout strategy using upper-band thrust, short RSI cross, and volume participation filters.
L1_medium.query: Buy when df['close'] > df['bb_upper_20'] AND df['rank_20'] > 0.80 AND df['vsumd_10'] > 0.40, with an additional trigger requiring a momentum cross: df['rsi_7'] > 50 AND yesterday df['rsi_7'] <= 50. Allow an alternate early-entry path using OR: enter if df['rsv_14'] > 0.85 AND df['cntd_5'] > 0.60 AND df['klen'] > 0.03. Exit on a momentum failure cross: df['rsi_7'] < 60 AND yesterday df['rsi_7'] >= 60, OR if df['close'] < df['bb_middle_20']. Enforce fixed take-profit and stop-loss using return windows: take-profit if df['roc_5'] >= 1.06, and stop-loss if df['roc_5'] <= 0.97. Add a fast crash-protection exit if df['qtld_20'] < -0.03.

L1_medium.summary: Fast breakout/power-candle entries with breadth and volume thrust filters, using wider fixed exits.
L1_medium.query: Buy when df['rsv_9'] crosses above 0.85, defined as df['rsv_9'] > 0.85 AND df['rsv_9'].shift(1) <= 0.85, AND df['vsumd_10'] > 0.30. Allow an alternate early-entry trigger using price action: (df['kmid2'] > 0.60 AND df['klen'] > 0.030) AND df['cntd_5'] > 0.60, even if df['rsv_9'] has not crossed. Take profit when df['rsi_7'] > 85 OR df['roc_3'] < 0.94 (roughly a >6% rise over 3 bars). Stop out when df['roc_3'] > 1.05 (roughly a >5% drop over 3 bars) OR df['kmid'] < -0.030.

L1_medium.summary: High-tempo breakout buy near 20-day highs with breadth and volume thrust, wide stops.
L1_medium.query: Buy when df['max_20'] <= 1.003 AND df['vma_20'] < 0.80 AND df['vsumd_5'] > 0.30 AND (df['cntd_5'] > 0.60 OR df['sumd_5'] > 0.50) AND df['rsi_6'] > 55 AND df['rsi_6'].shift(1) <= 55 (RSI crosses above 55). Set target exposure to 1.00 when the entry rule triggers. Sell when any of the following is true (OR): df['roc_3'] >= 1.06 (fixed stop-loss), OR df['roc_3'] <= 0.92 (fixed take-profit), OR df['rsi_6'] < 50 AND df['rsi_6'].shift(1) >= 50 (RSI crosses below 50), OR df['max_10'] >= 1.02 (price is at least ~2% below its 10-bar max, suggesting breakout failure).

L1_medium.summary: Dual-trigger approach combining trend resumption and pullback recovery, filtered by volatility and money flow.
L1_medium.query: Start from risk gating: only allow entries when df['atr_14'] < df['sma_20'] * 0.035 AND df['std_20'] < 0.060. Trigger A (trend resumption) is a price cross above df['sma_50'], defined as df['close'] > df['sma_50'] and prior bar df['close'] <= df['sma_50'], plus df['mfi_14'] > 55 AND df['sumd_10'] > 0.20. Trigger B (pullback recovery) is df['cci_20'] crosses above -100 (df['cci_20'] > -100 and prior bar df['cci_20'] <= -100) AND df['min_20'] < 0.97 AND df['rsi_14'] > 40. Generate an exit signal when df['qtlu_20'] > 0.04 OR df['roc_7'] < 0.97 (about a +3% move over 7 bars). Generate a stop exit when df['roc_3'] > 1.02 (about a -2% move over 3 bars) OR when df['cci_20'] crosses below 100 (df['cci_20'] < 100 and prior bar df['cci_20'] >= 100).

L1_medium.summary: EMA golden-cross entries with calm-volatility and non-extended price filters, tight ROC risk exits.
L1_medium.query: Enter a position only when a golden cross occurs: df['ema_20'] > df['ema_60'] AND df['ema_20'] shifted by 1 bar <= df['ema_60'] shifted by 1 bar. Require confirmation with df['rsi_14'] > 45 AND df['rsi_14'] < 65 AND df['std_20'] < 0.035 AND df['qtlu_30'] < 0.01. Exit on any of the following: a death cross (df['ema_20'] < df['ema_60'] AND df['ema_20'] shifted by 1 bar >= df['ema_60'] shifted by 1 bar) OR df['rsi_14'] > 72. Apply fixed risk exits every bar: take profit when df['roc_10'] < 0.97, and stop loss when df['roc_5'] > 1.015.

L1_medium.summary: Trend-following entry with RSI cross confirmation and strict SMA-based profit and loss exits.
L1_medium.query: The strategy seeks low-frequency, high-conviction entries aligned with a stable uptrend. Enter when df['close'] > df['sma_150'] AND df['sma_50'] > df['sma_150'] AND df['klen'] < 0.03 AND df['rsi_14'] crosses above 52 (today df['rsi_14'] > 52 AND the prior bar df['rsi_14'] <= 52), with a liquidity/quality confirmation of (df['vma_30'] < 0.95 OR df['mfi_14'] > 60). Take profit when df['close'] >= df['sma_50'] * 1.05 OR df['rsi_14'] > 72. Stop loss when df['close'] <= df['sma_50'] * 0.985 OR df['rsi_14'] crosses below 50 (today df['rsi_14'] < 50 AND the prior bar df['rsi_14'] >= 50). As an additional capital-preservation override, also exit whenever df['wvma_20'] > 1.50.

L1_medium.summary: Fast momentum entry on MACD cross with volatility and volume surge, using MA-ratio TP/SL.
L1_medium.query: Buy when df['macd'] crosses above df['macd_signal'] (today df['macd'] > df['macd_signal'] AND the prior bar df['macd'] <= df['macd_signal']) AND df['vma_10'] < 0.80 AND df['std_10'] > 0.03, and require a momentum thrust of (df['cci_20'] > 100 OR df['rsi_7'] > 60). Take profit at a fixed extension threshold when df['ma_5'] < 0.94 OR when df['imax_10'] < 0.05. Apply a hard stop loss when df['ma_5'] > 1.02 OR when df['macd'] crosses below df['macd_signal'] (today df['macd'] < df['macd_signal'] AND the prior bar df['macd'] >= df['macd_signal']). To avoid chasing climactic spikes, invalidate the entry on bars where df['kup2'] > 0.60.

L1_medium.summary: Two-regime entries driven by current volatility, with simple volatility-based sizing and fixed exits.
L1_medium.query: Exit discipline is fixed: take profit when df['close'] >= df['sma_20'] * 1.06 OR df['imax_20'] < 0.05, and stop loss when df['close'] <= df['sma_20'] * 0.97 OR df['rsi_14'] < 40. Use current volatility to set both behavior and size: if df['std_20'] < 0.03, use 1.0x size and enter on a pullback recovery where df['close'] > df['sma_100'] AND df['min_10'] < 0.95 AND df['rsi_14'] crosses above 45 (today df['rsi_14'] > 45 AND the prior bar df['rsi_14'] <= 45). If df['std_20'] >= 0.03, use 0.5x size and enter on active momentum where df['close'] crosses above df['sma_20'] (today df['close'] > df['sma_20'] AND the prior bar df['close'] <= df['sma_20']) AND df['cntd_10'] > 0.40 AND df['vma_20'] < 0.90. In either regime, require df['ksft2'] > 0.10 to avoid entries where the close is overly weak versus the bar’s range.

L2_easy.summary: Uptrend pullback entries with multi-confirmation and tight, volatility-aware risk exits.
L2_easy.query: The goal is to participate only in established uptrends and avoid drawdowns from unstable regimes. Require trend confirmation using df['close'] relative to a longer moving average (e.g., df['ema_50'] or df['sma_200']) and only allow entries when the faster average (e.g., df['ema_20']) is not below the slower average. Enter on a controlled pullback: df['rsi_14'] should be below a conservative “oversold-in-uptrend” threshold while price remains above the longer trend filter, and add a secondary confirmation such as df['mfi_14'] staying above a low “capitulation” level. Set position size conservatively: use a smaller allocation when only the pullback signal is present, and increase toward full size only when momentum confirmation agrees (e.g., df['macd'] > df['macd_signal']). Exit immediately on risk breakdown (e.g., df['close'] falling below the trend filter or closing below df['bb_lower_20']), and take profits when price reaches an upper-band stretch (df['close'] near df['bb_upper_20']) or df['rsi_14'] reaches an inferred overbought zone. Add a volatility gate using df['std_20'] so trades are avoided or downsized when volatility is elevated.

L2_easy.summary: Trade only established trends, filtered by low volatility and non-overbought momentum confirmation.
L2_easy.query: The objective is steady trend capture with strict risk control and low trade frequency. Generate an entry signal only when a short EMA is above a long EMA (use df['ema_{n1}'] > df['ema_{n2}'] with n1 < n2) AND volatility is calm (df['std_{n3}'] below a conservative cutoff) AND momentum is supportive but not stretched (df['rsi_{n4}'] in a neutral-to-bullish zone rather than overbought). Add a participation filter so signals are ignored on abnormal volume spikes (e.g., require df['vma_{n5}'] not to indicate extreme one-bar volume). Exit when trend quality deteriorates (close falls below a medium trend anchor such as df['sma_{n6}']) or when a volatility-based stop is hit (use df['atr_{n7}'] as the risk yardstick with a relatively tight multiple). Optionally take partial profits when price becomes extended versus df['bb_upper_{n8}'] while keeping the remainder only if the EMA trend condition still holds.

L2_easy.summary: Buy near 52-week highs in calm volatility, exit on volatility spikes or trend loss.
L2_easy.query: The objective is to participate only in high-quality uptrends while minimizing drawdowns. Enter when price is behaving like a “52-week high leader”: df['max_252'] is close to 1.0 (price near its 252-day high) and trend bias is positive via df['ma_100'] < 1.0 (price above its 100-day average). Add a risk filter that requires a volatility contraction using df['std_20'] below a conservative cutoff, and avoid chasing by requiring df['rsi_14'] to be strong but not “overbought” (pick a reasonable upper band). Exit on any sign of deterioration: price no longer near highs (df['max_252'] meaningfully above 1.0) or a volatility expansion (df['std_20'] jumps above its risk cutoff) or momentum loss (df['rsi_14'] falls below a neutral threshold). Use an ATR-based protective stop referenced to df['atr_14'] with a relatively tight multiple consistent with capital preservation, and size positions smaller when df['std_20'] is higher even if entry conditions are met.

L2_easy.summary: Exploit momentum bursts with volume surge and strong closes, riding until momentum fades.
L2_easy.query: Buy when a momentum burst is underway and the day closes with clear dominance. Define the burst using a short-horizon rate-of-change (df['roc_3'] or df['roc_5'] indicating strong upside), require trend agreement with a fast EMA above a slower EMA (e.g., df['ema_10'] > df['ema_30']), and confirm urgency with a volume surge via df['vma_20'] being meaningfully below 1.0 (current volume above average). To ensure you are not buying weak rallies, require a strong close location such as df['ksft2'] being high (close near the high of the bar), and allow entries even when oscillators are elevated (do not over-filter). Exit quickly when the thrust fails: df['macd_hist'] turns negative or df['rsv_14'] drops back below a mid-range “loss of control” level. L2_easy.summary: Trade only calm uptrends, entering on shallow pullbacks with strict volatility-based risk exits.

L2_easy.summary: Blend trend participation and pullback entries with volatility-adaptive sizing and volume-price alignment checks.

Enter when the tape shows a clean trend stack (a fast df['ema_{n}'] above a slow df['ema_{m}'], with df['sma_{k}'] also supportive) AND realized volatility is muted (df['atr_{n}'] or df['std_{n}'] below a calibrated stability threshold) AND volume flow is constructive (df['obv'] rising or df['mfi_{n}'] holding in a healthy zone rather than overbought/oversold extremes). Use conservative sizing by default; only scale up when all three pillars agree (trend alignment + volatility calm + flow confirmation), otherwise stay small or flat. Risk controls must be volatility-first: if df['atr_{n}']/df['close'] spikes or df['wvma_{n}'] jumps (interpreted as “impact cost / stress”), override any entry and cut exposure. Exit when trend integrity breaks (close slipping below a slow df['sma_{k}'] or df['ema_{m}']) or when flow rolls over (df['obv'] downshift / df['mfi_{n}'] deterioration), and define a protective stop distance as a multiple of df['atr_{n}'] inferred from the stock’s behavior.

L2_hard.summary: Buy volatility-compressed bases when liquidity dries up and downside pressure visibly fades.
L2_hard.query: The objective is to enter only after a selloff has transitioned into a low-stress base, interpreted as volatility compression (df['std_{n}'] and/or df['atr_{n}'] falling toward a low percentile for the chosen lookback) while “liquidity dries up” (df['vma_{n}'] elevated, implying current volume is below its recent mean). Trigger a buy when price regains a quality anchor (e.g., df['close'] crossing above df['bb_middle_{n}'] or df['ema_{n}']) AND a momentum gauge confirms selling exhaustion (df['rsi_{n}'] lifting out of an oversold region and/or df['cntd_{n}'] turning positive). Add a conservative validation that participation is not distributive by requiring df['corr_{n}'] to be non-negative (or improving), avoiding rebounds that occur on adverse price–volume association. Use a tight, volatility-aware risk rule: if df['close'] breaks below df['bb_lower_{n}'] by a small buffer or if a multiple of df['atr_{n}'] is exceeded to the downside, the target exposure must be zero regardless of other signals. Take profits quickly into mean reversion by reducing/closing exposure when df['close'] approaches df['bb_upper_{n}'] or when df['rsv_{n}'] indicates a stretched position near the top of its recent range; calibrate all thresholds and lookbacks to keep turnover low.

L2_hard.summary: Blend rejection-wick mean reversion with trend bias and volatility-adaptive exposure control.
L2_hard.query: This approach targets “absorption” dips that occur within a constructive trend backdrop, where trend is represented by df['ema_{n_fast}'] above df['ema_{n_slow}'] (or df['sma_{n}'] slope implied by price holding above it) while a pullback shows downside rejection (df['klow2'] elevated and df['ksft'] supportive). Enter on a dip toward support (df['close'] near df['bb_lower_{n}'] or below df['ema_{n_fast}']) only when money flow behavior is healthier than price momentum (df['mfi_{n}'] holding up relative to df['rsi_{n}'], or improving while df['rsi_{n}'] is still subdued), suggesting “smart buying” rather than panic. Make exposure volatility-adaptive on the current bar: reduce sizing when df['wvma_{n}'] or df['std_{n}'] is high (noisy tape) and allow larger sizing when both are muted, without relying on any regime state memory. Risk is gated by a participation veto: if df['corr_{n}'] turns meaningfully negative (price rising on unfavorable volume dynamics), the target exposure should be reduced or set to zero even if the entry setup is present. Exit into strength when df['close'] reverts to df['bb_middle_{n}']/df['ema_{n_slow}'] or when upside exhaustion appears (df['kup2'] elevated with df['rsv_{n}'] high), and enforce a protective stop based on a chosen multiple of df['atr_{n}'] to cap adverse excursions.

L2_hard.summary: Carry the primary uptrend while exiting quickly on volatility shocks and distribution cues.
L2_hard.query: The strategy targets quiet, durable trend carry and avoids paying up during stress. Define the trend as df['ema_{fast}'] > df['ema_{slow}'] and df['close'] > df['ema_{slow}'], then require “orderly tape” confirmation via a low-volatility filter such as df['std_{n}'] below a chosen ceiling and df['klen'] below an expansion threshold. Add a participation sanity check: require df['corr_{n}'] to be positive (or improving versus a chosen baseline) so price gains are not occurring on shrinking liquidity. Exit (risk-first) whenever a stress signature appears, such as df['atr_{n}'] rising above a chosen tolerance or df['klen'] jumping above its ceiling, and also exit on trend loss via df['close'] < df['ema_{slow}'] or df['macd_hist'] turning negative. Position sizing should be conservative and volatility-aware (smaller when df['atr_{n}']/df['close'] is elevated), with an optional extra reduction when df['rsi_{n}'] is already near an inferred overbought zone.

L2_hard.summary: Defensive trend participation gated by volatility calm and orderly price-volume alignment.
L2_hard.query: The objective is to participate only in “orderly tape” upswings while aggressively vetoing stress. Enter when df['close'] is above a medium/long trend anchor (e.g., df['ema_{n}'] and/or df['sma_{n}']) and the market shows calm risk conditions via low df['std_{n}'] and contained df['atr_{n}'] relative to recent behavior (thresholds and periods to be inferred). Require evidence that participation is constructive, such as df['obv'] trending upward and a supportive price–volume linkage (use df['corr_{n}'] or df['cord_{n}'] with a positive/strength threshold to be chosen). Use conservative, signal-strength sizing: smallest size when trend is positive but volume/flow confirmation is marginal, and larger size only when all confirmations align. Exit (and/or cut exposure) on “risk-off leakage,” defined by a volatility shock (df['std_{n}'] or df['atr_{n}'] jumping above its risk threshold) or a loss of trend support (df['close'] falling back below the chosen df['ema_{n}']). Take profits when the move looks stretched without healthy follow-through, e.g., df['close'] near/above df['bb_upper_{n}'] while df['rsi_{n}'] is in an overbought zone and volume confirmation weakens (exact levels to infer).

L2_hard.summary: Regime-aware blend: buy trend pullbacks or range dips with volatility-scaled exposure.
L2_hard.query: This approach first classifies the current bar as “trend-friendly” versus “mean-reverting” using a regime test built from df['ma_{n}'] (trend bias), df['imxd_{n}'] (directional range structure), and a volatility gauge such as df['std_{n}'] (periods and cutoffs to be inferred). In a trend-friendly regime, enter on controlled pullbacks: df['rsv_{n}'] falling into a lower zone while df['close'] remains above a chosen df['ema_{n}'], with a supportive flow filter from df['mfi_{n}'] improving or df['obv'] not diverging negatively (exact definitions to infer). In a mean-reverting regime, buy “discounted” prints near the lower envelope, such as df['close'] near/below df['bb_lower_{n}'] with df['rsi_{n}'] subdued and without a concurrent volatility spike. Position size should adapt to risk: scale down when df['std_{n}'] or df['wvma_{n}'] indicates turbulent trade quality, and scale up only when volatility is contained and the chosen participation filter (df['corr_{n}']/df['cord_{n}']) is favorable. Exits should differ by regime: trend mode exits on loss of the anchor (df['close'] under df['ema_{n}'] or df['ma_{n}'] reverting), while range mode exits on reversion toward df['bb_middle_{n}']/df['bb_upper_{n}'] or on oscillator normalization (specific thresholds to infer). Include a universal risk override that forces flat/very small exposure when a “shock bar” is detected via extreme df['klen'] together with elevated df['atr_{n}'] or df['std_{n}'].

L2_medium.summary: Volume-confirmed breakouts with momentum stacking and wider ATR stops to capture outsized runs.
L2_medium.query: Buy quickly when price transitions into a momentum breakout, accepting more noise to catch large directional moves. Use a breakout trigger defined by price pushing into the top of its recent range (df['max_{n}'] approaching 1.0) or closing above df['bb_upper_{n}'], and require momentum stacking via df['macd'] vs df['macd_signal'] and an oscillator strength condition (df['rsv_{n}'] and/or df['rsi_{n}'] above a bullish threshold). Confirm the breakout with participation: volume expansion relative to its average (df['vma_{n}'] indicating above-normal activity) and/or an improving accumulation proxy (df['obv'] rising), with exact cutoffs left to be inferred. Increase target exposure when multiple momentum/volume confirmations agree (e.g., MACD confirmation plus strong df['cntd_{n}'] or df['sumd_{n}']), and downshift when only the price breakout is present. Risk management should be looser than conservative styles: use a wider df['atr_{n}']-multiple stop and allow room for volatility, but force a hard exit when momentum fails (df['macd_hist'] flips negative or df['stoch_k_{n}'] crosses below df['stoch_d_{n}'] from a high zone). Add a “fast profit skim” rule: when momentum becomes stretched (e.g., df['rsi_{n}']/df['mfi_{n}'] extreme) reduce exposure even if the trend filter remains positive.

L2_medium.summary: Aggressive impulse-chasing using CCI and MACD thrust with volume surge and momentum exits.
L2_medium.query: Buy fast when an upside impulse is detected, prioritizing early momentum over perfect confirmation. Trigger an entry when df['cci_{n}'] surges upward from a depressed region and df['macd_hist'] flips positive or accelerates upward, with an added “thrust” filter such as df['stoch_k_{n}'] leading df['stoch_d_{n}'] and/or df['rsv_{n}'] breaking into its upper zone. Require a volume shock to validate the impulse using df['vma_{n}'] dropping below a surge threshold (current volume meaningfully above its recent average), optionally reinforced by df['logvol'] being elevated versus its recent norm via df['vstd_{n}']. Use signal-strength sizing: take a smaller allocation when only one momentum component confirms (e.g., MACD thrust without CCI thrust), and a larger allocation when momentum + volume conditions align simultaneously. Exit quickly on momentum failure (df['macd_hist'] turning down, df['stoch_k_{n}'] crossing below df['stoch_d_{n}'], or df['rsi_{n}'] rolling over from an overheated zone), but allow wider room via an ATR-based risk buffer (df['atr_{n}']) to avoid being shaken out of strong trends.

L2_medium.summary: Capitulation-candle dip buys with volume shock confirmation and wide ATR stops for rebound capture.
L2_medium.query: Buy when a “capitulation and snapback” signature appears: an unusually large candle range (df['klen'] above a high-percentile threshold) with a pronounced lower rejection tail (df['klow2'] elevated) and improving close location (df['ksft'] turning upward or df['kmid'] positive). Demand a concurrent volume shock to validate urgency, using current volume versus its average (df['vma_{n}'] well below 1.0) and/or a surge in volume volatility (df['vstd_{n}'] above a chosen floor). Add an early confirmation trigger from oscillators: df['rsi_{n}'] and/or df['mfi_{n}'] rebounding from extreme-low territory, with additional confidence if df['imin_{n}'] indicates the recent low occurred very recently (argmin near the end of the window). Use aggressive sizing that scales up when the candle rejection + volume shock + oscillator rebound all agree, but scales down when only one of these components fires. Set a wider stop using a larger multiple of df['atr_{n}'] to avoid being shaken out, and exit into strength when the move becomes crowded/extended (e.g., df['rsv_{n}'] reaches an upper zone and df['stoch_k_{n}'] enters overbought), or when statistical stretch (df['qtlu_{n}']) becomes meaningfully positive and momentum fades (df['sumd_{n}'] rolls over).

L2_medium.summary: Trade only calm uptrends with participation confirmation, exiting quickly on instability signals.
L2_medium.query: The objective is to participate in established uptrends while avoiding noisy, high-risk periods. Enter when trend structure is bullish (e.g., df['ema_{short}'] > df['ema_{long}'] and df['close'] is above df['sma_{long}']), volatility is subdued (df['std_{n}'] and/or df['atr_{n}'] relative to df['close'] below a conservative threshold), and participation confirms the move (df['cord_{n}'] positive and current volume above its typical level using df['vma_{n}'] below a set cutoff). Add a “chop filter” that blocks entries when price is too mid-range (df['rank_{n}'] near the center of its range) or when df['bb_upper_{n}'] and df['bb_lower_{n}'] are too tight/wide relative to the intended calm regime. Exit defensively on any trend damage (df['close'] falling back below df['ema_{long}'] or df['ema_{short}'] slipping under df['ema_{long}']) or on a risk shock (df['atr_{n}'] spikes above a set volatility ceiling). Take profits conservatively when price becomes extended (df['close'] approaches df['bb_upper_{n}'] and df['rsi_{n}'] reaches an overbought zone), prioritizing capital preservation over squeezing the last increment.

L2_medium.summary: Exploit momentum acceleration using EMA stacking and speed metrics, with wider ATR-based risk limits.
L2_medium.query: Buy when the tape shows acceleration rather than waiting for deep pullbacks: require a bullish moving-average stack (df['ema_{fast}'] > df['ema_{mid}'] > df['ema_{slow}']) plus a momentum kick identified by df['roc_{n}'] shifting decisively to the “above 1.0” side and df['beta_{n}'] turning strongly positive. Use a lightweight confirmation that the move is being fueled, not fading, such as df['rsi_{n}'] holding above a midline threshold and df['vsumd_{n}'] or df['cntd_{n}'] indicating more up-days / up-volume than down. Increase exposure when multiple acceleration components align (EMA stack + strong df['beta_{n}'] + favorable df['vsumd_{n}']), and scale down when only the EMA stack is present without speed. Exit quickly on loss of thrust (df['beta_{n}'] rolling below a chosen floor, or df['macd_hist'] turning negative) and use a wider stop based on df['atr_{n}'] to tolerate volatility while targeting outsized runs. Add a stretch-based profit capture rule when df['qtlu_{n}'] signals price is unusually rich versus its upper quantile, even if the trend remains positive.

L2_medium.summary: Regime-aware drift versus snapback using volatility filters and adaptive exposure sizing.
L2_medium.query: This approach switches behavior based on the current bar’s volatility regime, aiming for steady returns without excessive turnover. Classify regime using df['std_{n}'] (price volatility) together with df['vstd_{n}'] or df['wvma_{n}'] (volume/impact noise), with thresholds selected to separate calm from turbulent conditions. In calm regimes, trade “drift” by requiring persistence signals such as df['cntd_{n}'] > 0 and df['corr_{n}'] > 0, plus a mild trend alignment like df['ema_{fast}'] > df['ema_{slow}'] or df['ma_{n}'] < 1.0; enter when these agree. In turbulent regimes, trade “snapback” by buying statistically depressed price states (df['qtld_{n}'] sufficiently negative and/or df['min_{n}'] near 1.0) only if money flow stabilizes (df['mfi_{n}'] above a chosen floor) to avoid catching weak bounces. Exposure should be volatility-scaled: smaller size when df['std_{n}'] is high, larger size when df['std_{n}'] is low, with an additional haircut when df['wvma_{n}'] indicates unstable impact. Exit drift trades on deterioration (df['cntd_{n}'] turning negative or df['close'] slipping under df['ema_{slow}']) and exit snapback trades into normalization (df['qtlu_{n}'] turns positive or df['close'] reaches df['bb_middle_{n}']/df['bb_upper_{n}']). Add a simple throttle to reduce churn by requiring df['rank_{n}'] to be above a minimum percentile for drift entries and df['rsv_{n}'] to be sufficiently low for snapback entries, with cutoffs inferred.

L2_medium.summary: Trade post-compression band reversion within a higher-timeframe uptrend, with strict risk limits.
L2_medium.query: The strategy targets low-risk entries after volatility compression, only when the broader trend is supportive. Define a trend filter using a longer-term moving average pair (e.g., df['sma_{n}'] and df['ema_{n}']) so trades are allowed only when price and/or the faster average are above the slower average. For entry, require a “quiet base” condition using depressed df['std_{n}'] and price behavior near the lower Bollinger region (df['bb_lower_{n}'], df['bb_middle_{n}']), then trigger on a reclaim of the Bollinger midline with confirmation that df['obv'] is not falling (accumulation/absorption). Add a chop-avoidance filter using a mid-range oscillator (df['rsi_{n}'] or df['mfi_{n}']) to avoid entering when momentum is already extended. Exit primarily on a mean-reversion objective toward df['bb_upper_{n}'] or on momentum stalling (oscillator rolling over), with a tight volatility-based stop tied to df['atr_{n}'] and a time-based exit if price fails to progress within a chosen bar limit.

L2_medium.summary: Exploit early momentum ignition via thrust candles, participation breadth, and volume surprise confirmation.
L2_medium.query: Buy when an “ignition bar” appears: a wide-range bullish candle (high df['klen'] and strongly positive df['kmid2']) that closes near the high (low df['kup2']) to indicate urgency. Demand participation confirmation using a short-window upside breadth metric (df['cntp_{n}'] or df['sumd_{n}']) alongside a volume surprise condition where current volume is materially above its recent mean (df['vma_{n}'] sufficiently below 1) and/or volume change pressure is positive (df['vsumd_{n}'] > 0). Add a momentum continuation check such as df['macd_hist'] improving versus its recent value or a favorable price/volume change linkage via df['cord_{n}'] being positive. Position sizing should be aggressive when multiple thrust components align (candle strength + breadth + volume), but reduced when only the candle trigger is present. Use a wider ATR-based stop (df['atr_{n}']) to tolerate noise, and take profits via a momentum “exhaustion” cue (e.g., df['cci_{n}'] reaching an extreme and starting to fade or df['stoch_k_{n}'] entering a high zone) rather than waiting for a full reversal.

L2_medium.summary: Defensive re-entry after selloff exhaustion using CCI/MFI recovery and volatility risk gates.
L2_medium.query: The strategy targets low-frequency, high-conviction rebounds after a controlled selloff, prioritizing capital preservation. Enter when an exhaustion-and-stabilization cluster appears: df['cci_{n}'] reverses upward from an extreme negative zone, df['mfi_{n}'] confirms improving buy pressure, and price reclaims a nearby trend anchor such as df['sma_{n}'] (or df['ema_{n}']). Require a risk gate so entries only occur in “orderly” conditions, e.g., df['std_{n}'] and/or df['atr_{n}'] are below a conservative cutoff to avoid catching volatile cascades. Position size is signal-strength based: smaller exposure on the initial CCI/MFI turn, and larger exposure only when both the moving-average reclaim and a supportive volume posture (e.g., df['vma_{n}'] easing, or df['obv'] no longer deteriorating) agree. Exit defensively if price loses the reclaimed average or if df['cci_{n}'] rolls over, and take profits when momentum reaches a defined overbought/extended state (e.g., df['cci_{n}'] high or df['rsi_{n}'] high). Add a “staleness” twist: if the recent-high recency metric df['imax_{n}'] indicates the rally is aging without fresh highs, de-risk or exit even if price has not broken down.

L2_medium.summary: Low-volatility trend continuation using middle-band reclaim plus participation and volume-quality filters.
L2_medium.query: The objective is to participate only in orderly advances and avoid noisy, distribution-heavy rallies. Enter when df['close'] is above a longer-term trend anchor (use df['ma_{n}'] < 1 as the “price above mean” test) and df['close'] is also above df['bb_middle_{n}'], while a calm-market filter holds (df['std_{n}'] below a conservative threshold you select). Require participation confirmation by insisting df['cntp_{n}'] is high and df['corr_{n}'] is non-negative, so price strength is not occurring on weak volume behavior. Size modestly by default, and only allow a larger allocation when df['sumd_{n}'] and df['vsumd_{n}'] are both clearly positive (choose the cutoffs). Exit defensively if df['close'] falls back under df['bb_middle_{n}'] or if df['cord_{n}'] turns sufficiently negative (distribution signal). Take profits sooner when df['qtlu_{n}'] becomes meaningfully positive or df['rsi_{n}'] reaches an upper-zone threshold you define, to reduce exposure to overextension.

L2_medium.summary: Regime-adaptive approach: trend-following in calm markets and rebound entries during high-volatility pullbacks.
L2_medium.query: This approach switches behavior using a current-bar volatility regime test: treat the market as high volatility when df['std_{n}'] or df['atr_{n}'] is elevated (pick the lookbacks and thresholds), otherwise treat it as low volatility. In low-volatility regime, enter on trend strength via df['ema_{fast}'] > df['ema_{slow}'] with df['rank_{n}'] in an upper band you set, while avoiding overbought extremes by requiring df['rsi_{n}'] below a ceiling you define. In high-volatility regime, look for washed-out pullbacks: df['min_{n}'] near 1.0 (price near its rolling low) combined with an oscillator turn such as df['stoch_k_{n}'] > df['stoch_d_{n}'] and df['mfi_{n}'] recovering above a low threshold you select. Position size should be volatility-scaled on the current bar (smaller when df['atr_{n}'] or df['wvma_{n}'] is large), with a cap to prevent oversized exposure in turbulent conditions. Exit rules should match the regime: in low volatility, exit on trend break (df['ema_{fast}'] < df['ema_{slow}'] or df['macd_hist'] < 0); in high volatility, exit into mean reversion (df['close'] reaching df['bb_middle_{n}'] or df['rsi_{n}'] returning to a midline zone you choose). Add a fail-safe risk exit in either regime if df['qtld_{n}'] becomes materially negative (statistical downside extension), overriding any entry bias.

L2_medium.summary: Multi-confirmation trend participation with volatility gating and disciplined mean-reversion exits.
L2_medium.query: The strategy seeks low-frequency entries by only participating in established uptrends, using a moving-average stack such as df['close'] above a slower df['sma_{n}'] and a faster df['ema_{n}'] above a slower df['ema_{n}']. Entries are taken only on “controlled pullbacks,” defined as price retreating toward df['bb_middle_{n}'] (or slightly below) while momentum does not fully break down (e.g., df['rsi_{n}'] holding above an oversold zone) and money flow remains constructive (df['mfi_{n}'] above a neutral midpoint or improving). Add a chop/fragility filter: skip signals when realized volatility is elevated (df['std_{n}'] high versus a longer-window df['std_{n}']) or when price–volume coupling is unhealthy (df['cord_{n}'] negative). Risk control should be tight and volatility-aware, with the stop distance defined as a conservative multiple of df['atr_{n}'] and position size reduced as df['atr_{n}'] or df['std_{n}'] increases. Exits prioritize capital preservation: close the trade if df['close'] falls back below the chosen trend EMA/SMA, if df['mfi_{n}'] rolls over below its midpoint, or if df['rsi_{n}'] enters an overbought zone and price tags df['bb_upper_{n}'] (profit-taking).

L2_medium.summary: Fast momentum ignition using MACD acceleration and quantile expansion with volume-skew confirmation.
L2_medium.query: Enter quickly when momentum “ignites”: require df['macd_hist'] to flip positive and expand while price shows an upper-tail expansion signal via df['qtlu_{n}'] moving above its neutral line (choose the lookback). Add a participation thrust check using df['vsumd_{n}'] (or df['vsump_{n}']) turning strongly positive to confirm that volume changes skew toward up moves, but do not require a long-term trend filter so the strategy can catch early breakouts. Increase position size when multiple momentum components agree (e.g., df['macd'] above df['macd_signal'] plus strong df['qtlu_{n}']) and reduce size when the volume confirmation is weak or df['vstd_{n}'] signals noisy flow. Use a wider, volatility-aware stop based on df['atr_{n}'] to tolerate shakeouts, but enforce a fast “breakout failure” exit when df['macd_hist'] contracts back toward/under zero or df['qtlu_{n}'] reverts sharply. Add a time-sensitivity proxy without state by exiting on the first clear loss of impulse (e.g., df['kmid'] turns decisively negative together with weakening df['vsumd_{n}']).

L2_medium.summary: Trend-aligned dip-buying with volatility and volume-stability filters plus defensive exits.
L2_medium.query: The objective is steady upside capture while prioritizing drawdown control through strict trade filtering. Enter on a pullback in an established uptrend: require price above a longer-term trend anchor (choose from df['sma_{n}'] or df['ema_{n}']) while a shorter-term average remains supportive, then buy only when momentum is merely “cooling” (e.g., df['rsi_{n}'] in a moderate range, not deeply oversold or overbought). Add a capital-preservation gate that blocks entries during turbulence by using a low-volatility filter (df['std_{n}'] and/or df['atr_{n}'] relative to price), and require stable participation via a volume-quality constraint (df['vstd_{n}'] low and/or df['vma_{n}'] not signaling abnormal churn). Position size should be smaller by default and scaled down further when volatility measures rise, even if the trend filter is positive. Exit defensively when the trend is threatened (close falling back below the chosen trend anchor) or when downside expansion is detected (close under df['bb_lower_{n}'] or a clear deterioration in df['mfi_{n}']). Include an additional “early abort” rule that exits quickly on signs of distribution such as df['obv'] weakening while price is still near the entry zone, with the exact sensitivity left to calibration.

L2_medium.summary: Volatility-regime switching between trend riding and quantified mean reversion with adaptive sizing.
L2_medium.query: When volatility is subdued versus its own recent baseline, operate in trend-following mode: require a bullish moving-average structure (pick df['ema_{fast}'] above df['ema_{slow}'] or price above df['bb_middle_{n}']) and validate with participation quality using df['cntd_{n}'] or df['sumd_{n}'] to avoid weak, drift-only rallies. If the current bar indicates a high-volatility regime (elevated df['std_{n}'] and/or df['atr_{n}']), switch to mean-reversion mode and look for statistical stretch: prefer df['qtld_{n}'] materially negative or price near df['bb_lower_{n}'], paired with reversal-friendly candle geometry (e.g., high df['klow2'] or improving df['ksft2']). Position sizing must adapt to risk: scale down as volatility rises, but allow moderate size in calm regimes when trend and participation align. Exits should be mode-specific: in trend mode, exit on loss of structure (close back below the chosen EMA/band midline) or weakening participation (cntd/sumd reverting); in mean-reversion mode, exit into normalization (return toward df['bb_middle_{n}'] or qtld mean-reverting) and cut quickly if the stretch worsens (further quantile downside or volatility spike). Add a single, consistent safety override across both modes that forces risk-off when volume becomes erratic (df['vstd_{n}'] spikes) even if price signals look attractive.

L2_medium.summary: Trend-qualified dip entries with volume participation confirmation and volatility-based de-risking exits.
L2_medium.query: The strategy prioritizes capital preservation by only engaging when the stock is in a clearly defined primary uptrend, using a long-horizon moving-average filter (e.g., df['ema_{n_long}'] and/or df['sma_{n_long}']) and requiring price to remain above that trend anchor. Look for a controlled pullback into a “value zone” defined by Bollinger structure (df['bb_middle_{n_bb}'] to df['bb_lower_{n_bb}']) while momentum is washed out on a short oscillator (df['stoch_k_{n_stoch}'] vs df['stoch_d_{n_stoch}'] and/or df['rsi_{n_rsi}']) without showing panic-level volatility. Demand participation confirmation before entry via positive volume skew (df['vsumd_{n_vol}'] above a modest threshold) and/or improving price–volume correlation (df['corr_{n_corr}'] above a minimum), so dips are bought only when activity supports accumulation. Risk control must override everything: if realized volatility expands (df['std_{n_std}'] or df['atr_{n_atr}'] relative to price exceeds a set ceiling), reduce exposure or block new entries. Exit on a defensive break of the trend anchor (close falling below df['ema_{n_long}']/df['sma_{n_long}']) or on a mean-reversion completion signal (price reverting to df['bb_middle_{n_bb}']/df['bb_upper_{n_bb}'] with oscillator reaching a defined “overbought” zone), and include an ATR-based stop distance that is intentionally tight for this profile.

L2_medium.summary: Low-volatility trend participation using Bollinger reclaims, money-flow confirmation, and defensive volatility gating.
L2_medium.query: The objective is to participate only when conditions are calm and directional, prioritizing drawdown control. Enter when price is in an uptrend defined by a longer-term df['sma_{n}'] (or df['ema_{n}']) filter, and df['std_{n}'] is below a conservative “quiet-market” threshold while df['vstd_{n}'] is also muted. Require a constructive re-entry signal such as df['close'] reclaiming df['bb_middle_{n}'] after being near df['bb_lower_{n}'], with money-flow confirmation via df['mfi_{n}'] above a neutral midpoint and not deteriorating. Position size should be small by default and increase one step only when both df['corr_{n}'] (price vs log-volume correlation) is positive and df['wvma_{n}'] indicates stable traded-risk (i.e., not elevated). Exit immediately on a defensive break (e.g., df['close'] falling below the trend filter or below df['bb_lower_{n}']), and take partial profits when df['close'] approaches df['bb_upper_{n}'] alongside an overbought oscillator condition (RSI or Stochastic). L2_medium.summary: Trend-biased value entry using quantile pullbacks, volume-coupling confirmation, and volatility-scaled exposure tiers.

L2_medium.summary: Buy capitulation-wick dips within a primary uptrend, exiting quickly on normalization signals.

L2_medium.summary: Participate in calm uptrends using trend confirmation, stable volume, and volatility-based de-risking.

L2_medium.summary: Validated trend participation using MA alignment, money-flow confirmation, and strict volatility gating.

L2_medium.summary: Exploit early momentum ignitions using MACD thrust, oscillator cross, and expansion-candle confirmation.

L2_medium.summary: Blend trend participation with volatility-aware dip entries, scaling exposure by current risk conditions.

L3_easy.summary: Low-turnover pullback-to-trend entries with strict downside control and time-based exits.
L3_easy.query: Target steady profitability with capital preservation as the primary constraint, accepting fewer trades to avoid low-quality signals. Enter only when a higher-timeframe uptrend filter is positive and price is in a controlled pullback (not a breakdown), then require a bullish reversal trigger plus a secondary confirmation from either improving momentum or supportive volume behavior. Use a tight, clearly-defined invalidation: exit immediately on a failed reversal (e.g., price losing the pullback reference level or momentum rolling back over) and do not re-enter unless the full setup reappears. Add a time-based exit to avoid “dead money” exposure: if price does not progress within a limited holding window, close the position. Take partial profits on a sharp favorable move to reduce risk, then keep the remainder only while trend conditions remain intact. Impose a hard maximum drawdown limit and a conservative maximum position size per signal.

L3_easy.summary: Risk-adjusted approach blending trend participation and tactical dip-buying with volatility-scaled exposure.
L3_easy.query: Optimize profit potential while maintaining stable risk-adjusted performance, avoiding both over-trading and overly selective entries. Determine a simple market condition on each bar using current-bar measures of trend persistence versus choppiness and current volatility level; use this to choose between two behaviors: trend-follow entries in directional conditions and mean-reversion entries after controlled pullbacks in non-directional conditions. In the trend mode, require alignment between a trend filter and positive momentum; in the range mode, require an oversold/washed-out signal plus evidence of stabilization before entering. Size positions adaptively: increase exposure when volatility is low-to-moderate and signal strength is high, and cut exposure when volatility is elevated or signals conflict. Exits should combine a protective stop (price/volatility-based) with a profit-taking rule and a time stop, so trades either work promptly or are closed. Add a portfolio-level constraint: limit maximum drawdown and keep turnover within a moderate band by requiring fresh confirmation before any new entry.

L3_easy.summary: Capital-preserving swing strategy emphasizing downside caps and selective, high-conviction entries.
L3_easy.query: Design a single-stock strategy whose primary objective is capital preservation while still compounding gains over time. Generate entry signals only when multiple independent conditions align via threshold-based rules or factor comparisons drawn from the provided price/volume and precomputed indicator columns. Impose a strict per-trade loss limit and a portfolio-level drawdown cap that, when breached, forces an immediate flat signal regardless of any entry criteria. Keep turnover low by requiring strong confirmation and by enforcing a minimum time separation between new entry signals. Include a conservative profit-taking rule that locks in gains early unless the price action continues to validate the trade, and add a time-based exit so stagnant trades are closed even without hitting stops.

L3_easy.summary: High-velocity upside capture with frequent signals, scaling rules, and wide but explicit risk limits.
L3_easy.query: Build a single-stock strategy with one overriding objective: maximize total return by capturing fast upside expansions. Use threshold and crossover-style comparisons to trigger frequent entries as soon as early strength appears, even at the cost of more false positives. Require an explicit risk budget: a wide initial stop framework plus a hard maximum drawdown limit that overrides all other logic. Add a scaling-in mechanism that increases exposure when the current-bar evidence of acceleration strengthens, and a rapid “fail-fast” exit condition when the move loses thrust. Constrain the strategy with a maximum holding time to recycle capital quickly, and specify a high-activity expectation (many trades) while still respecting the drawdown cap.

L3_easy.summary: Fast-reacting momentum hunter that scales into strength and exits on rapid invalidation.
L3_easy.query: Build a strategy with the single objective of maximizing upside capture during strong advances, accepting a higher false-signal rate. It should trigger entries early in emerging moves, using permissive thresholds and/or fast crossovers, and allow frequent re-entries when conditions reappear. Require an explicit rule for scaling up exposure when the move strengthens, while still defining a maximum exposure limit to prevent runaway risk. Use wider risk limits than conservative approaches, but add a clear “fast failure” exit when the initial thrust does not follow through. Take profits using a rule that lets winners run while still forcing exit when momentum clearly degrades.

L3_easy.summary: Defensive dip-buying that only engages after controlled selloffs and swift stabilization.
L3_easy.query: The objective is to compound steadily while prioritizing capital preservation and avoiding deep drawdowns. Define entries only when a broader uptrend is confirmed, the stock experiences a sharp pullback consistent with a temporary dislocation, and evidence of stabilization appears via improving internal momentum and supportive volume behavior. Require at least two independent confirmations that include both a price-to-trend comparison and a bounded oscillator threshold, so weak bounces are filtered out. Risk controls must dominate: if any volatility-stress or downside-momentum warning condition triggers on the current bar, the strategy must reduce exposure or stay flat even if entry conditions are partially met. Exits should be conservative and fast: close positions on trend invalidation, renewed downside acceleration, or a clear reversal in the stabilization signals. Keep trading frequency intentionally low by demanding high-quality alignment rather than frequent signals.

L3_easy.summary: High-tempo upside capture focused on impulsive strength, gaps, and momentum continuation.
L3_easy.query: Buy when the current bar shows an impulsive bullish price action pattern (e.g., strong close and expansion relative to recent range) that aligns with a fresh upside acceleration signal. Confirm the trigger using a momentum trend measure and a volume/flow confirmation so that weak “pop-and-drop” moves are avoided. Position sizing should be opportunistic: increase exposure as signal strength rises (e.g., stronger impulse and stronger confirmation yields larger allocation), while still enforcing a hard risk budget per bar. Exits must be designed to tolerate noise but respond decisively to failed continuation—use a reversal/weakness condition that reflects momentum stalling, adverse candle structure, or a breakdown back into the prior congestion zone. Allow relatively frequent re-entries as long as the same impulse-and-confirmation template appears, but apply a strict rule that any risk-warning condition overrides new entries on that bar. The strategy should explicitly aim for outsized winners by letting strong trends run until objective deterioration signals appear.

L3_easy.summary: High-activity momentum capture with rapid entries, scaling, and looser but structured risk limits.
L3_easy.query: Buy quickly when early momentum appears, even if confirmation is incomplete, with the goal of capturing large directional moves. The strategy should favor breakout and acceleration behavior and allow multiple re-entries when strength persists, subject to a clear signal threshold or crossover logic chosen by the designer. Use position scaling: start with a meaningful base allocation and add exposure as the move strengthens, while defining an explicit maximum exposure ceiling. Risk controls should tolerate noise (wider stop-loss) but enforce a hard cut on sharp reversals and a daily/weekly loss limit that disables new entries when breached. Include an exit that locks gains during strong runs (e.g., trailing protection or partial profit-taking) to avoid round-tripping extended moves. Keep trading frequency intentionally high, but require a liquidity filter so signals are only acted on when participation is sufficient.

L3_easy.summary: Exploit fast momentum bursts with early entries, rapid re-entries, and a wide-but-structured risk framework.
L3_easy.query: Build a high-return strategy aimed at capturing large upside bursts, accepting a higher false-signal rate as the cost of speed. Signals should trigger early using threshold/comparison logic on the available indicators, with a bias toward reacting to sudden acceleration and strong follow-through rather than waiting for prolonged confirmation. Require an explicit high activity constraint (e.g., permit frequent signals and allow immediate re-entry after an exit if conditions reappear), while still enforcing a hard daily/weekly loss limit to prevent runaway losses. Use a wider initial risk allowance than a conservative approach, but mandate a dynamic exit that tightens as price moves favorably (e.g., a trailing invalidation based on current-bar conditions). Position sizing must be allowed to expand when the current-bar signal quality strengthens, subject to a strict maximum exposure cap at all times.

L3_easy.summary: Blend trend participation with selective pullback entries, using volatility-based sizing and disciplined exits.
L3_easy.query: Target robust profitability with a balanced mandate: moderate drawdowns, moderate turnover, and avoidance of extreme tail-risk days. Use two complementary entry pathways: (1) trend-following entries when the prevailing direction is supported by improving momentum, and (2) pullback entries when price shows a controlled retracement that stabilizes without renewed downside pressure. Calibrate position size continuously from current volatility (larger size in calmer conditions, smaller size in noisier conditions) while respecting a fixed maximum exposure cap. Exit on either a predefined loss limit, a predefined profit capture rule, or a clear invalidation of the entry rationale (trend break for pathway 1, stabilization failure for pathway 2). Add a simple “do-not-trade” constraint when market conditions appear directionless or excessively volatile to reduce churn.

L3_easy.summary: Low-turnover, capital-preserving entries requiring aligned trend, momentum, volatility, and volume confirmation.
L3_easy.query: Objective: achieve steady positive returns while prioritizing capital preservation over trade frequency. Define entry signals only when multiple independent confirmations align, expressed as clear threshold rules and/or crossovers between at least two available indicators (e.g., a trend component plus a momentum component) with an additional liquidity/volume sanity check. Risk constraints: target a maximum peak-to-trough drawdown of 8% and cap average trading frequency to no more than 6 round trips per month.
